subject: Aurora Retail — token budget slices & continuous-batching assumptions
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Patrick Lopez <patrick.lopez@aurora-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on yesterday's call — token sizing & batching

Hi Patrick — thanks again for the call. Capturing the notes and the only asks we left with: 

1) Confirm target budget band ($/1M tokens) you want us to size to — you mentioned a mid-range target on the call.
2) Share a 48-72h traffic sample (CSV) with per-request token counts and timestamps so we can model continuous batching.
3) Confirm peak concurrency expectations (typical and burst).

High-level assumptions we plan to validate if you don't object (we'll run sims once we have the sample):
- Continuous batching window: 40ms default (we'll test 20/50/100ms).
- Expected average request length: 120–220 tokens (you said ~150 on the call).
- Typical steady concurrency: 8–30 concurrent requests; bursts up to ~120 for promo spikes.
- Target latency SLO: 250ms p95 (please confirm).

Preliminary unit economics model we used for the call (top-level):
- Model cost basis: $/1M tokens (inference + infra).
- If target is $12/1M tokens => estimated monthly (60M tokens) ~= $720 / month in compute-only inference charges (simplified calc for sizing).

Next steps: Patrick to send sample CSV; Monica to run batching sim and return per-bucket batch sizes + latency delta; Marissa to prepare a pricing slice (target, optimistic, conservative).

Attachments: please attach the 48–72h sample when convenient. I attached the high-level calc workbook in advance.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_token_econ_calcs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 68 KB)]

From: Patrick Lopez <patrick.lopez@aurora-retail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on yesterday's call — token sizing & batching

Hi Rafael — thanks, this is great. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget target: aiming for $10–$14 per 1M tokens. Our CFO likes $12 as a planning point.
- Monthly volume: rough steady state 60M–110M tokens; seasonally we may spike to ~180M for 48h during promos.
- Typical prompt+completion: ~150 tokens; only 8% of calls are >400 tokens.
- Concurrency: steady 10–25; bursts up to 140 (short lived, <5m).
- Latency SLO: prefer p95 < 250ms for user-facing features; p99 < 600ms acceptable for async backfills.

I'll attach a 72-hour traffic extract (anonymized) within 2 business hours. One question on billing: how do you treat cached prefixes and repeated completions? Do they deduct from token billing if served from KV cache?

Thanks — Patrick
Patrick Lopez
Head of AI, Aurora Retail
[Attachment: aurora_72h_sample.csv (csv, 42 KB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Patrick Lopez <patrick.lopez@aurora-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T17:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on yesterday's call — token sizing & batching

Appreciate the quick turnaround and sample — got it. Short answers while Monica and Marissa dig in: 

- Caching & billing: prefix/KV cache reduces compute and therefore effective token cost per request; billing is still per token generated but we can model hit-rate adjusted effective $/1M tokens for you (e.g., 20% cache hit => apparent cost drops proportionally).

- For continuous batching: when a request is satisfied entirely from cache (full hit) there is no model token billing; partial hits still bill for generated tokens. We'll include an explicit column in the sim for cache-hit scenarios.

Attached is a quick walk-through of the unit-econ calc with the numbers you gave; I used $12/1M as the planning point and show three scenarios (steady, promo spike, conservative). If you want we can present a one-pager showing run-rate committed pricing for Dedicated pools vs Hoste d (usage).

Action: Monica — please run the batching sim on the attached 72h CSV and return projected p95 latency and per-1M-token cost bands for these three scenarios. Marissa — can you draft a 3-slice pricing recommendation (target $12, aggressive $10, conservative $14) and note when Dedicated starts becoming materially cheaper (monthly token thresh).

Rafael
[Attachment: aurora_72h_sample.csv (csv, 42 KB)]
